Yinyang appendices

Psychological readings

Psychological conflict, belief and reasoning, and interaction research offer ways to understand how people experience, interpret, and respond to their lives. For ordinary users, this repository's route is for the model to work with philosophy and personal material to help form and revise an understanding of the person. The person contributes experience, purposes, recognition, and correction. Psychological research and professional methods are collected at the end.

Links lead to publisher records, samples, author materials, or public full texts.

Psychological conflict, relationships, and change

As environments and relationships change, earlier wishes, commitments, and habits can pull against new circumstances. These readings address ambivalence about change, competing needs, self-criticism and protection, love and hostility toward the same person, and knowing something without being able to act on it. Different theories explain these phenomena through their own concepts and evidence.

More accessible books

Author and book Reading entrance
Russ Harris, The Happiness Trap, second edition (2022) A general-reader entrance to acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT): entanglement with thoughts and feelings, values, and action. More approachable than beginning with its theoretical manual.
Richard C. Schwartz, No Bad Parts (2021) A general-reader entrance to Internal Family Systems (IFS), using parts and their protective roles to understand self-criticism and internal opposition.
Jeffrey E. Young and Janet S. Klosko, Reinventing Your Life An accessible schema-oriented account of recurring life patterns, needs, and coping, illustrated through cases. Pair with the professional schema-therapy text below.
Karen Horney, Our Inner Conflicts A classic entrance to the tensions among moving toward, against, and away from others. Read its diagnostic vocabulary in its historical context.

Contemporary psychotherapy: understanding conflict and change

These readings cover approaches developed in recent decades and their updated textbooks, including theory, cases, and dialogue.

Approach and representative book Question to bring to the reading
ACT: Hayes, Strosahl, and Wilson, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, second edition; Harris, ACT Made Simple, second edition Professional theory and a more accessible practice introduction. How can action follow values without first eliminating inner experiences? Focus on psychological flexibility, defusion, acceptance, and committed action.
DBT: Marsha M. Linehan, DBT Skills Training Manual, revised edition (2025) A professional skills-teaching manual. How can acceptance and change coexist? Examine mindfulness, interpersonal effectiveness, emotion regulation, and distress tolerance. The companion handouts are a separate volume.
Schema therapy: Young, Klosko, and Weishaar, Schema Therapy: A Practitioner's Guide A professional text on needs, early schemas, coping, and modes in recurring internal and relational conflicts. Pair with the accessible Reinventing Your Life.
IFS: Schwartz and Martha Sweezy, Internal Family Systems Therapy, second edition (2019) A professional text on opposition, relationships, and change among protective parts; chapter 11 specifically addresses protector polarizations.
Emotion-focused therapy: Leslie S. Greenberg, Emotion-Focused Therapy: Coaching Clients to Work Through Their Feelings, second edition A professional text on emotional functions and expression, self-criticism, unfinished relational experience, and emotional transformation. This entry refers to Greenberg's emotion-focused approach.
Motivational interviewing: William R. Miller and Stephen Rollnick, Motivational Interviewing, fourth edition (2023) For helping professions and practitioners. Follow ambivalence about changing and reasons to retain the present arrangement through engaging, focusing, evoking, and planning.
Coherence therapy and memory reconsolidation: Bruce Ecker, Robin Ticic, and Laurel Hulley, Unlocking the Emotional Brain, second edition (2024) Advanced theory and cases concerning conflict between explicit wishes for change and implicit emotional learning. Distinguish reconsolidation research, the authors' clinical interpretation, and evidence for particular methods.
Mentalizing: Carla Sharp and Dickon Bevington, Mentalizing in Psychotherapy (2022) A professional introduction with dialogues and cases. How do people understand their own and others' mental states under relational strain while keeping interpretations revisable?

Classic conflict theories and psychoanalysis

Author and original work Reading purpose
Freud, Introductory Lectures, Lecture XXIII; The Ego and the Id Historical theoretical accounts of compromise between opposing tendencies and pressures among identifications, reality, and the ego ideal.
Freud, Mourning and Melancholia Examine how love, hostility, identification, and self-reproach are related in the explanation.
Melanie Klein, Notes on Some Schizoid Mechanisms (1946) The trust's original-work reading entrance. Examine splitting, projection, and different aspects of the same object alongside the earlier depressive-position account.
D. W. Winnicott, Playing and Reality; Ego Distortion in Terms of True and False Self Transitional space between creation and encounter, and the relationships among compliance, spontaneity, and true/false self.

For Freud, Lacan, and philosophical discussions of will and self-deception, see philosophical readings.

Belief and reasoning

These references address belief revision, information access, and reasoning, connecting formal rules, particular situations, and actual change.

Paper or reference Reading purpose
Logic of Belief Revision Use AGM and related frameworks to distinguish expansion, contraction, and revision, while keeping formal rationality distinct from a person's actual changes.
Dynamic Epistemic Logic Compare information events, knowledge and belief states, and updates, including public announcements and other information events.

Research on conflict, fragmentation, and dynamic revision

Paper Further question
Elga and Rayo, Fragmentation and Information Access A 2019 author manuscript of the 2021 chapter. How does possessing information differ from accessing it now, and how are beliefs organized across contexts?
Grodniewicz (2024), Belief Revision in Psychotherapy A philosophical paper on why a new understanding in one setting may not generalize to another.
Mansell and Huddy (2020), Computational Models of Psychological Change and Recovery Theory and simulations: how can conflict and reorganization be represented when goals impose incompatible references on the same controlled variable?
Kronemyer and Bystritsky (2014), A Non-Linear Dynamical Approach to Belief Revision in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy A theoretical proposal connecting dynamics with belief revision.

Interaction research

These studies address meaning, coordination, epistemic trust, and learning in relationships.

Paper Content
De Jaegher and Di Paolo (2007), Participatory Sense-Making Include interaction, coordination, and sense-making in an explanation; ask what separate descriptions of participants' internal states might omit.
Fonagy and Allison (2014), The Role of Mentalizing and Epistemic Trust in the Therapeutic Relationship Institutional manuscript entrance. Connect understanding mental states, epistemic trust, and social learning.

Psychological research and professional methods

Professional references on case formulation, experiential material, and language-model research.

Case formulation and psychodynamics

Book or chapter Content and source
The Psychodynamic Formulation Collective, Psychodynamic Formulation: An Expanded Approach (2022) A professional textbook on psychodynamic formulation, including development, conflict and defense, relationships, self, sociocultural context, and collaborative formulation. The publisher provides a contents list and first-chapter sample.
Nancy McWilliams, Psychoanalytic Diagnosis, second edition (2011) A professional conceptual and case textbook on psychoanalytic personality theory, defenses, and relational organization, with publisher contents and a sample.
Tracy D. Eells, Psychotherapy Case Formulation, second edition (2026) A case-formulation textbook addressing explanatory hypotheses, quality, and clinical application. The link leads to the APA publisher record.
Jacqueline B. Persons and Michael A. Tompkins, Cognitive-behavioral Case Formulation (2007) A chapter in Eells's edited Handbook of Psychotherapy Case Formulation, second edition, pp. 290–316. Author institution's bibliography · Author-uploaded chapter.

Experience and individual differences

Book or paper Content and source
Braun and Clarke (2006), Using Thematic Analysis in Psychology A foundational qualitative-methods paper addressing theoretical positions, analytic choices, and patterns in material.
Oblak et al. (2024), Crisis of Objectivity An open case study constructing an individualized network from experiential material to understand connections among difficulties.
Mischel and Shoda (1995), A Cognitive-Affective System Theory of Personality A theory of situations, cognitive-affective relations, and behavioral variation, including “if–then” behavioral signatures.
Navarro and Foxcroft, Learning Statistics with jamovi (2025) An open textbook covering measurement, research design, descriptive statistics, sampling and estimation, correlation, and regression.

Research methods and model explanation

Book or paper Content
Borsboom et al. (2021), Theory Construction Methodology Psychological theory construction and the relationships among data, phenomena, explanations, and formal models.
Jhangiani et al., Research Methods in Psychology, fourth edition An open textbook covering hypotheses, qualitative research, observation, cases, measurement, and research design.

Language models and personal understanding

Research Subject and available material
Hossain et al. (2025), AutoPsyC · Code Recognizing psychodynamic conflicts in semi-structured interviews, comparing prompting, retrieval, and fine-tuning.
Hu et al., TheraMind · Code Research on a longitudinal counseling agent, evaluating cross-session information and strategy adjustment through simulated conversations.
Zhou et al. (2026), ReaLMem and ChronoProfiler A benchmark and profiling study of long-term multimodal personal archives, distinguishing factual recall, persona inference, and predictive personalization.

Related work includes Vazire (2010) on self–other knowledge asymmetry, Peters, Cerf, and Matz (2024) comparing GPT-4 personality inferences with self-report Big Five measures, and Burger et al. (2022) connecting case formulation with Bayesian idiographic networks in Clinical PREMISE.
